summary: On Sunday 20 July 2008 Amazon S3 degraded for hours after a few server-to-server messages had a single flipped bit that stayed readable but carried wrong state, which spread through the gossip protocol. Amazon had to shut down all server-to-server communication and request processing, clear state and restart.

overview.background: S3 servers shared system state by gossip. Customer data was checked with MD5, but internal state messages had no equivalent check.
systems: S3 servers and the gossip protocol
Request processing in the US and EU
overview.impact: S3 requests failed or were degraded for several hours (the card says several hours).
overview.severity: A long outage that needed a full shutdown and restart of the system.
overview.gaps: The AWS status page (the card source) could not be read. Facts come from Werner Vogels's post and Data Center Knowledge.

diagrams.title: A bad message spreads and cannot be un-spread
diagrams.caption: Per the reports, a flipped bit in a few state messages spread through gossip, and with no check on internal state the corruption went unnoticed until the whole system had to be cleared.

timeline.e: A few messages with a single flipped bit begin to spread through gossip.
Servers have trouble communicating and requests fail or degrade.
Engineers decide to shut down all server-to-server communication and request processing, clear system state and restart.
Communication and request processing are stopped and state is cleared.
Internal communication is restored and request processing restarts in the US and EU.
Amazon adds checksums, gossip monitoring and faster restart.

rootCause.trigger: Single-bit corruption of internal state messages distributed by gossip.
rootCause.underlying: Customer data was protected by MD5, but internal state messages had no equivalent check.
contributing: Restart of the whole system takes long

evidence.label: Werner Vogels on the root cause
evidence.body: Root cause was single bit corruption of internal state messages that are distributed via Gossip techniques.

evidence.label: A simulated checksum
evidence.body:
import zlib
msg = b'node-17:state=up:epoch=42'
framed = msg + zlib.crc32(msg).to_bytes(4, 'big')
assert zlib.crc32(framed[:-4]).to_bytes(4, 'big') == framed[-4:]
evidence.note: A way to frame a message with a checksum. Not Amazon's code.

diagnose.step: Look at whether servers agree on state.
Check if any message integrity checks exist.
Decide if a full reset is the only option.

fix.safety: Never restart with state that may be corrupt. Clear it first.

troubleshoot.scenario: A gossip protocol carries a corrupt state message and all servers now hold wrong state. Customer data is intact.
troubleshoot.question: What is your plan?
troubleshoot.answer: Stop communication, clear internal state, restart in stages, then add checksums and alarms.

options: A single flipped bit in internal state messages

design.prompt: Design a gossip protocol that tolerates corruption.
design.answer: Checksums, authenticated messages, rate limits on state change and a rehearsed reset.

checks.q: What time did request processing start restarting?
